articles.summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more about AI's impact on the web, follow Emma Roth. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started The digital publishing industry has relied on […]

articles.title: In first-ever climate crisis amends, Nepal to get $21.6 million
articles.summary: The decision taken this week by the UN body, the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), in its emergency meeting assumes significance as it is not only a kind of admission that climate change causes such extreme events, but also an endorsement of the principle that historical polluters (developed nations) must contribute to the fund to assist vulnerable developing countries.

articles.title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs 'thrown' at idol during procession
articles.summary: Hindu organisations protested following an incident where eggs were allegedly thrown at a Durga Mata idol. The incident occurred during an immersion procession within Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad. Police responded promptly after receiving a call and took the suspects into custody for investigation. A similar incident involving stone-pelting was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra.

articles.title: Protests engulf Europe: People take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
articles.summary: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. Demonstrations were reported in France, Italy, Albania, Spain, and Portugal, with varying degrees of violence. Clashes between protesters and police resulted in numerous arrests and injuries in several countries. Many demonstrators called for affordable housing, better education, and protection of public pensions.

articles.title: ‘200 seats haq hai hamara’: Congress puts its UP poll ambitions on Lucknow walls
articles.summary: Posters demanding 200 Assembly seats have surfaced outside the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee headquarters in Lucknow. Congress aims to strengthen its position ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections by negotiating a larger seat share. The party has reportedly submitted a wishlist to its ally, Samajwadi Party, complicating seat-sharing discussions. State Congress leaders are using a grading model to evaluate constituencies based on organisational growth.

articles.title: Who is Gadi Eisenkot? Ex-army chief of Israel is Netanyahu's biggest challenger
Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan shift donations towards AI and science
articles.summary: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan are investing $50 million to establish STEM labs and an AI center at Sacramento State University. This generous donation aims to transform vacant state office buildings into a thriving downtown campus. California Governor Gavin Newsom emphasized this initiative will enhance the tech job talent pipeline, while the couple shifts their philanthropic efforts toward biomedical AI, aligning with Meta’s vision for innovation and education.

articles.title: ‘JD(U) is finished’: Bihar strongman Anant Singh to float own party after expulsion
New York court orders review of jailed mother's $500 child support cap claim
articles.summary: A New York woman serving a seven-year prison sentence for kidnapping her child has won a fresh hearing over unpaid child support. Chelsea Four-Rosenbaum had sought to limit her debt to $500, arguing that her income remained below federal poverty guidelines while imprisoned. An appeals court ruled that her request had been examined under the wrong legal provision and ordered a fresh review.

articles.title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 48,056 crore in October as market selling continues
articles.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors have withdrawn Rs 48,056 crore from Indian equities during October due to high crude oil prices. Selling eased slightly in a recent week, with some FPIs becoming net buyers for two days. Elevated oil prices and inflation concerns are contributing to deteriorating corporate earnings outlooks affecting investor confidence. Domestic institutional investors have somewhat mitigated the selling pressure on markets in recent weeks.

articles.title: 'When will you score runs?' Babar Azam's weaknesses exposed by ex-Pakistan player
articles.summary: Babar Azam's recent performances in the ODI tri-series have raised concerns regarding his ability to convert starts into significant scores. He scored 45 against Sri Lanka and 34 against England, failing to build on important beginnings. Former cricketer Tanveer Ahmed has highlighted weaknesses in Babar's batting against spinners, incoming fast deliveries, and short balls. He emphasized the need for Babar to address these vulnerabilities to improve his performance.

articles.title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to support local artisans by prioritizing their products while shopping for festivals. He emphasized that doing so would strengthen the 'Vocal for Local' campaign and promote a self-reliant India. Modi highlighted successful local exports such as makhana and arhar dal to various international markets. Additionally, he discussed efforts aimed at reviving traditional skills and farming practices, including natural cotton cultivation.

articles.title: Kentucky court orders fresh review of $703,000 farm dispute after divorce
articles.summary: Mary and Fred Holden's property settlement agreed to equal ownership of their Kentucky farm. Disagreements arose regarding when the farm should be listed for sale after two years. After their son moved out, Mary requested the farm be sold or purchased by Fred. The appeals court found the agreement's wording ambiguous, requiring a fresh evaluation in family court.

articles.title: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis expand $10M beach house after mudslides
articles.summary: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are planning a significant renovation of their Carpinteria beachfront property. The proposed changes include expanding the main residence and adding a swimming pool. They acquired the property in 2017 for $10.1 million and have seen its estimated value rise to about $17 million. The couple's plans involve the removal of a guest cottage to enhance the outdoor living space.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says US rules pushed China toward self-reliance
articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang pointed out that US export controls have significantly fueled China's semiconductor advancements. He remarked that these restrictions have compelled China to bolster its own chip production strengths. Huang also expressed strong faith in the US technology sector's resilience, despite heightened competition from China, and dismissed worries about an impending memory chip surplus, predicting ongoing demand for High Bandwidth Memory in the years ahead.

articles.title: IIT Madras graduates' hostel idea grows into over 1,500 foldable buildings
articles.summary: Modulus Housing, founded by IIT Madras graduates, focuses on manufacturing foldable buildings for quick assembly and transportation. Since 2018, it has provided over 1,500 modular structures across India and parts of Africa. The startup aims to improve access to essential infrastructure like schools and clinics, especially in rural areas. Recently, it raised ₹70 crore in funding to support further expansion and innovation.

articles.title: From unfinished books to 10-second reels: Is reading becoming lost art?
articles.summary: The growing preference for short-form digital content is raising concerns about children’s ability to engage with books and sustain attention. Educationists and experts examine declining reading habits, the role of examination-driven learning, and the impact of digital distractions. Drawing on research and Kerala’s library movement, the story explores ways to rebuild deep reading through schools, families and communities.

articles.title: Drone attack: Iran targets Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq
articles.summary: Iran's armed forces conducted a drone attack on the Komala group in Iraq's Kurdistan region. This operation reportedly caused significant damage and casualties to the group's infrastructure. Previous strikes on the Komala group have occurred since the regional conflict began in February. Iran accuses these opposition groups of receiving support from Israel, its longstanding adversary. The Kurdish opposition has denied allegations of receiving arms from Israel despite Iran's claims.

articles.title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 cr from investors
articles.summary: Between October 26 and October 29, five companies will debut their initial public offerings, aiming to raise an impressive Rs 2,600 crore from the primary market. These firms—EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, M K Sons Fine Jewels, BLS Polymers, and Bombay Coated and Special Steels—will utilize the capital for business expansion, working capital augmentation, and settling debts. More companies are gearing up for IPO launches set for November 5.

articles.title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after protests over hydropower project
articles.summary: The Centre has deployed two Rapid Action Force companies comprising around 250 CRPF personnel to Arunachal Pradesh following violent protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.

articles.title: Man spits gutkha from 3rd-floor balcony, dies after coming in contact with 11kV wire
articles.summary: Prabhulal Gupta, a 65-year-old man, tragically died in Ganjbasoda after an apparent accident involving an overhead power line. Residents reported that his spit, while chewing gutkha, made contact with the 11kV line. Locals expressed anger towards the electricity company for neglecting their complaints about unsafe wiring. His landlord mentioned that officials had assured residents about addressing these high-tension line concerns.

articles.title: ‘Failed to pay rent’: How landlord’s complaint led to 1,600 fake Rs 500 notes
articles.summary: After a complaint from a concerned landlord, the Wathoda police raided a rented apartment, revealing a trove of counterfeit Rs 500 notes, printing machinery, and a laptop. Preliminary findings suggest that this operation may be connected to an extensive counterfeit currency syndicate. The principal suspect, Pushpam Bhandane, remains at large, prompting a coordinated search effort involving the anti-terrorism squad and other investigative bodies.

articles.title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises
articles.summary: In his latest statements, external affairs minister S Jaishankar called for a more robust leadership from the UN to confront pressing world issues. He highlighted a significant gap in global decision-making that leaves many regions, particularly in the Global South, behind in critical areas like finance, fuel, food, and fertilizer. Emphasizing the importance of fair AI development, Jaishankar encourages strategies that ensure widespread access to its benefits, fostering international cooperation.

articles.title: From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.

articles.title: Trump claims US has secured Greenland, Venezuela in ‘greatest real estate deal’
articles.summary: Donald Trump asserted at a rally that the United States has secured Greenland and Venezuela as territories. His statements were made despite the lack of legal transfer of sovereignty over Greenland from Denmark. A recent memorandum of understanding focused on maritime cooperation, which does not include Greenland. Trump also announced a significant investment by Audi in Georgia, emphasizing job creation.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces fresh setback as neighbors object
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.

articles.title: ‘Buy me Thar’: Woman slapped, kicked, dragged by hair by husband over vehicle demand
articles.summary: A 28-year-old woman has taken the brave step of reporting her husband after an alleged assault sparked by a dispute over a vehicle. CCTV footage depicts the disturbing encounter, while neighbors came to her aid upon hearing her screams. Police are currently eyeing the medico-legal report as they prepare to move forward with the case.

articles.title: Stock market outlook: Fed meeting, crude & more - top cues guiding Dalal Street this week
articles.summary: As Dalal Street braces for a pivotal week, key earnings reports and the impending US Federal Reserve interest rate decision are grabbing attention. Investors are eagerly anticipating the September industrial production and manufacturing figures, set to be released on October 28. Moreover, Jio Platforms' stock market entry promises to sway investor sentiment.

articles.title: Watch: Protesters launch fireworks at police as fiery clashes take place in Albania
articles.summary: Protests in Tirana escalated into clashes as demonstrators faced off with riot police during an anti-government rally. Protesters expressed their anger over alleged government corruption, unemployment, and education issues. The demonstrations also targeted government buildings and banks, leading to significant unrest in the city. The student-led protests represented a wider movement against corruption and called for governmental reforms.

articles.title: Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan hit back after KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal failures
articles.summary: India A struggled initially but found stability through an unbeaten partnership between Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan. Padikkal scored 56 runs, while Sudharsan contributed 39 runs, helping the team recover. After a poor start, the duo added 96 runs without losing another wicket by the end of Day 2. Earlier, India's bowlers did well as Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi took three wickets each.

'Not less than a pilgrimage’: PM Modi marks 12 years of Mann Ki Baat - top quotes

articles.summary: On November 1, Rahul Gandhi is set to lead a rally to rally citizens against alleged vote theft, spotlighting issues like voter list inaccuracies and the response to complainants. The BJP has voiced concerns over the timing due to its proximity to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots memorial. Several organizations, including Delhi's Chamber of Trade and Industry, have expressed disapproval.

articles.title: Judge who awarded 36 death sentences in 16 months transferred to family court
articles.summary: Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar has been transferred to the family court after awarding multiple death sentences. He gained national attention for his decisions in Muzaffarnagar, including a notable case of a husband burning his wife. His tenure included recalling numerous pending cases, raising questions regarding administrative authority. Diwakar previously faced threats following his involvement in a high-profile mosque survey case.

articles.title: Toddler killed by 24-yr-old elder brother inside Bihar temple
articles.summary: A one-and-a-half-year-old boy was allegedly murdered inside a Durga temple in Patna district. The accused, Ajit Kumar, is the elder brother of the victim, Manish Kumar. Police believe that Ajit used a sharp agricultural tool in the commission of the crime. Investigators are examining the motive and circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. Evidence is being collected to establish a clearer picture of the events that occurred.

articles.title: 'He was a fish out of water': Sooryavanshi's No. 3 role questioned after 2nd T20I
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin feels Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struggled at No. 3 in India’s second T20I against New Zealand, scoring just four runs off eight balls. He believes Sanju Samson should bat at No. 3 if Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma and Samson play together. Ashwin also praised India’s middle order, highlighting the power and temperament of Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ramandeep Singh.

articles.title: Clashes break out at Jamia protest, campus shut, classes go online
articles.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia has opted for an online class format and closed its physical campus amid escalating student protests. Demonstrators are campaigning for the reinstatement of their student union, which has been non-existent since 2006. Tensions soared when security forces reportedly used aggression against hunger strikers. The administration has asked students to halt protests, following unsuccessful dialogue attempts, with the campus remaining shut for safety.

articles.title: Chethan Kumar writes in Parallax: Why IISc should be Isro’s JPL
articles.summary: IISc and Isro have collaborated on various projects relevant to India's growing space ambitions. The partnership has included developing technologies relevant to spacecraft and exploring microbial life in space. A model similar to JPL could allow IISc to contribute more significantly to Isro's missions. Establishing a strong research framework is essential for such collaboration to mature over the years.

articles.title: People of 15 societies in Noida stage protest over pollution
articles.summary: Residents say developers are flouting dust norms and want heavy vehicles diverted through Pushta Road

articles.title: 6 children among 12 injured in shooting near Florida university stadium
articles.summary: A shooting occurred near a football stadium in Tallahassee during homecoming weekend at Florida A&M University. At least 12 individuals were injured, which included six children, and 11 had gunshot wounds. Authorities reported that three victims suffered serious injuries, with one critically injured and eight stable. The police chief indicated an altercation had preceded the shooting, but no arrests have been made.

articles.title: KL Rahul's horror show: Duck followed by bizarre hit-wicket dismissal
articles.summary: KL Rahul struggled in the first unofficial Test against New Zealand A, scoring only four runs in two innings. In the first innings, he was dismissed for a duck after edging a catch to the wicketkeeper. His second innings ended in a bizarre hit-wicket dismissal as he accidentally struck the stumps with his bat. Rahul's two failures contributed to India A's batting collapse in the match.

articles.title: Operation Trident: Rs 100 cr hawala transactions exposed, 18 arrested in drug crackdown
articles.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah announced Operation Trident, which targeted an international narcotics cartel in India. The operation, conducted in Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur, uncovered significant hawala transactions and led to arrests. Authorities froze numerous bank accounts and seized illegal items, including detonators and cash. Shah emphasized the government's commitment to eradicating drug networks by December 31, 2029.

articles.title: 'No target beyond reach': How Op Sindoor delivered 'crippling blows' deep inside Pak
articles.summary: IAF chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh said Operation Sindoor demonstrated that “no target was beyond its reach”, citing calibrated strikes spanning 1,200km across and 200km deep. In an interview with PTI, he praised indigenous weapons, precision targeting and integrated air defence, while stressing the need to strengthen combat capabilities, electronic warfare, AI-enabled systems and domestic defence production.

articles.title: 'Ignore strike calls': LPG distributor body ahead of Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi
France’s economic woes: Debt nears 122% of GDP, growth forecast at just 0.4%
articles.summary: France is grappling with severe economic challenges, marked by soaring public debt nearing 122% of GDP. With government expenditure exceeding 57% of the nation's economic output, the forecast of just a 0.4% growth raises concerns over financial stability. Protests centered on the rising cost of living showcase deeper political fractures. As the presidential succession nears, the economy stands as a pivotal issue for the electorate.

articles.title: Iran claims control of Strait of Hormuz, says 2 oil tankers hit mines, warns US warships against Persian Gulf entry
articles.summary: Iran claims control over the Strait of Hormuz and says two oil supertankers carrying over 4.5 million barrels struck naval mines. The claims remain unverified as Tehran warns US warships against entering the Persian Gulf amid fears of a US strike.

articles.title: Noida Sector 125 fire: Blaze at hotel spreads to nearby eateries, firefighting ops underway | Video
articles.summary: A fire at Krishna Food Point in Sector 125 on Saturday spread to nearby eateries, causing panic. Firefighters deployed four vehicles and brought the blaze under control with police assistance. No casualties were reported.

articles.title: Fodder scam case: CBI nabs Satyendra Kumar, accused on the run for 25 years from Lucknow station; all you need to know
articles.summary: The CBI arrested fodder scam accused Satyendra Kumar at Lucknow railway station after 25 years on the run. Traced to Nepal before returning to India, he is being brought to Ranchi on transit remand to face court proceedings.

articles.title: ‘838’ number plate, pool of blood, screams: Chilling video captures daylight murder
articles.summary: In a shocking act of violence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, bystanders witnessed a murder as Devesh Dixit was pursued and collided with a vehicle. His friend-turned-assailant, Pawan Parashar, went on to deliver a fatal blow using a stick and iron rod. The police arrived shortly after, and Parashar voluntarily surrendered later at the station. Investigations continue to reveal the motive behind this brutal attack.

articles.title: Burnt body of Class 12 student found behind guard room at Delhi school
articles.summary: An 18-year-old girl was discovered burnt behind the guard room of a school in Krishna Nagar. Police received a call regarding the fire incident and promptly arrived at the scene. They conducted preliminary proceedings and collected materials from the spot, including the victim's school bag. A crime team thoroughly inspected the location to gather evidence for the ongoing investigation.

articles.title: 'Why Nov 1?' BJP questions Rahul over rally date coinciding with 1984 riots anniversary
When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
articles.summary: Sonia Gandhi officially joined the social media platform X to share personal memories and insights. In her first post, she introduced her upcoming memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love. The memoir recounts her life experiences, including her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge. Scheduled for release on November 10, the book details her journey through love and loss.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos’s parents bet $245,573 on Amazon; their early stake worth billions today
'Please stop': J&K CM flooded with messages from MLAs as cabinet reshuffle in 2-3 days
Kentucky court rejects bid to use neighbour's driveway after land split
articles.summary: In a Kentucky court case, Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearns faced a setback in their property dispute against neighbors John and Betty Warinner. The Stearnses asserted that their long-term use of a pathway should grant them an implied easement. However, the jury found alternative access routes viable, leading to the dismissal of their claim, a verdict affirmed by the appeals court, confirming that historical usage doesn’t automatically legitimize easements.

articles.title: Watch: Two Philippine air force trainer aircraft collide mid-air; 4 pilots killed
Tilak Varma breaks world record during India vs New Zealand 2nd T20I
articles.summary: Tilak Varma achieved a historic milestone by taking the most catches in T20 Internationals during 2026. His remarkable performance included two catches in the second T20I against New Zealand. Varma surpassed the previous record held by Danilson Hawoe with a total of 26 catches this year. India won the toss and opted to bowl, making two changes to their playing XI.

articles.title: Megan Thee Stallion-backed project delivers over 2,200 care packs to Black girls
articles.summary: In January 2024, 12-year-old Mila Henry founded MH Boxes, aiming to support Black girls facing mental health challenges. With a $550 grant from the #BlackGirlJoyChallenge, she crafted care packages containing essential self-care items. To date, the initiative has successfully distributed over 3,300 boxes nationwide, striving to break the stigma surrounding mental health in the Black community.

articles.title: New York court revives privacy claim over cameras filming family's backyard
articles.summary: A couple in New York found themselves entangled in a complex property disagreement with their neighbors regarding a disputed land boundary tied to a chain-link fence. This conflict escalated, resulting in claims of trespassing and invasion of privacy due to surveillance cameras. Although the court struggled to rule on the boundary dispute, it has permitted the couple's privacy claims to advance for further scrutiny.

articles.title: As Tesla promotes product Musk predicted 80% of value will come from, costs jump
articles.summary: Elon Musk has announced the start of production for Tesla's humanoid robot, named Optimus, in Fremont, California. The production phase is still in its early stages and might experience challenges. Despite a decline in revenue from Tesla's solar and energy storage business, there is positive growth in its services sector. Musk estimates the company could manufacture 20,000 robots per week by the end of 2027.

articles.title: Denied library entry as boy, he helped open one; graduates rose from 4 to 30
articles.summary: Faced with caste discrimination when trying to access a library, V Selvakumar took matters into his own hands by starting a project to create one in Semmadu village. The result? A remarkable leap in educational achievement, with graduates rising from four to thirty. The local community, including youth and officials, rallied to sustain the library, emphasizing the transformative power of equitable educational access.

articles.title: 'Trump will take his dream to his grave': Iran says won't allow US warships in Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran has expressed its determination to prevent US military presence in the Persian Gulf amid escalating tensions. US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack mentioned the potential for a US strike on Iran this weekend. Despite threats, Barrack stated that President Trump continues to seek a diplomatic agreement. Trump emphasised that further military action remains a possibility if negotiations do not progress.

articles.title: How Jeffrey Epstein became Houthis' new weapon against Saudi Arabia
Did Van Gogh’s ‘Starry Night’ depict real sky from July 1889? Scientists think so
articles.summary: In a groundbreaking study, South Korean researchers have pinpointed July 22, 1889, as a possible date for the celestial scene depicted in The Starry Night. This new timeline disputes the widely accepted June 1889 date. The study notes that the alignment of stars aligns with observations from that evening, bolstered by van Gogh's letters that reference weather conditions, suggesting the artist's keen attention to his surroundings.

articles.title: 'Four years, I never chased this jersey': Bhuvneshwar Kumar on India comeback
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar credited patience, preparation and a no-expectations mindset for helping him return to international cricket after four years. The 36-year-old said the IPL and domestic cricket kept him sharp while improving his maturity. He also discussed modern T20 challenges, stressing that bowlers need smart strategies. India's strong start against New Zealand, he added, could boost confidence throughout the tour.

articles.title: ‘Noise protest’ rocks Manipur valley districts, police fire tear gas
articles.summary: In a powerful display of unity, thousands of demonstrators took to the streets in various valley districts of Manipur, articulating their concerns over the escalating crisis. Using traditional means of noise-making, they called for urgent government intervention. Key demands included the establishment of the National Register of Citizens and an improved response to ethnic tensions, showcasing a strong public insistence for accountability and resolution.

articles.title: 13k Pilibhit voter details changed, UP CEO calls it a ‘deliberate crime’
articles.summary: In a significant turn of events, an FIR has been filed against two SDMs and a voter registration operator due to allegations of fraudulent voter roll modifications. This manipulation has impacted more than 13,150 voters in the Pilibhit assembly constituency. The Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer emphasized the intentional nature of this act, calling it a crime rather than negligence.

articles.title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians (MI) have roped in former Rajasthan Royals high-performance coach Steffan Jones as a bowling consultant for their development squad. Jones will work with MI's development squad alongside director of performance Zubin Bharucha, with the duo tasked with helping Indian players improve their skillsets.

articles.title: Australian umpire's Ranji sojourn: Planes overhead at Palam, BKC's red soil pitch
articles.summary: Australian umpire Ben Treloar is experiencing Indian domestic cricket for the first time as part of the BCCI-Cricket Australia exchange programme. From aeroplanes flying overhead at Delhi's Palam ground to Mumbai's red-soil pitch at BKC, the 44-year-old shares his impressions of Indian first-class cricket, the warmth of its people and his growing love for local cuisine, including garlic naan and vada pav.

articles.title: IND vs NZ: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in playing XI, but there's a twist
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl first against New Zealand in the second T20. The team made two changes, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi replacing Ishan Kishan and Prince Yadav coming in for Mayank Yadav. Iyer emphasized the importance of maintaining their aggressive approach while addressing fielding improvements. New Zealand also made a change, bringing in Jacob Duffy for Adam Milne.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim Jong-un makes surprise visit to China via newly opened bridge
Husband’s illicit relationship by itself is not cruelty: Madras high court
articles.summary: Madras high court ruled that a husband's illicit relationship is not sufficient for cruelty under Section 498A. This ruling came from a case involving a woman who committed suicide with her child. The court noted that more evidence is required to establish cruelty beyond mere allegations of an affair. The trial court had acquitted the husband due to insufficient evidence linking him to dowry harassment.

articles.title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
articles.summary: US consumer sentiment has declined slightly as rising prices related to the Middle East conflict affect households' financial views. The Consumer Sentiment Index fell marginally to 48.0 in October, approaching a record low. Independents reported significantly weaker sentiment while Democrats and Republicans showed improvements. Inflation expectations rose, suggesting concerns about future price increases among consumers. The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain current interest rates during their upcoming meeting.

articles.title: 'Rs 10k cr at risk': Traders' body urges Rahul to defer Delhi rally amid Diwali season
India script history with best-ever finish and record 114 medals at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: India concluded the Asian Para Games 2026 with an extraordinary display of talent, amassing a total of 114 medals, consisting of 30 gold, 35 silver, and 49 bronze. This achievement surpasses their previous record from 2022 edition, securing a commendable fourth place overall. The rise of India's para-athletes on the continental stage was evident, even as China led with an impressive 217 gold medals.

Woman medical officer assaulted, slapped and abused in police presence; video viral

The accused was reportedly under the influence of alcohol when he attacked the doctor. Medical officers in Wardha district protested by boycotting work, highlighting safety concerns for healthcare personnel. Subsequently, police registered a case against the accused based on the medical officer's complaint.

articles.title: As foam builds up in Yamuna, questions raised over how work was allotted
articles.summary: A defoaming operation is set to begin in Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj, with equipment already in place. The Aam Aadmi Party has raised concerns about the tender allocation process favoring a specific contractor. Allegations state that the contractor set up equipment before the bids were officially opened. Delhi Jal Board representatives clarify that they have conducted defoaming campaigns annually since 2022.

articles.title: Watch: Iran shows Trump behind bars on live billboard on busy Tehran street
11-year-old Indian-origin prodigy Bodhana breaks Polgar's 38-yo record
articles.summary: Eleven-year-old British chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has become the youngest female player to qualify for the International Master title, breaking Judit Polgar’s 38-year-old record. The English Chess Federation praised her as a “generational talent.” Already the youngest Woman Grandmaster qualifier, Bodhana has achieved several historic milestones and is now aiming to become a Grandmaster, chess’s highest title.

articles.title: Watch: Paris shops increase security, board up windows, as France braces for protests
articles.summary: Shopkeepers in Paris are taking measures to secure their businesses against possible renewed protests and violence. Authorities are increasing police presence, with around 70,000 officers deployed this weekend across France. Demonstrations are planned in several cities, amidst ongoing political tensions leading to protests against rising living costs. While some support the protests, others condemn the associated looting and vandalism.

articles.title: Mumbai Indians appoint Kieron Pollard as head coach ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: Kieron Pollard has been named the head coach of Mumbai Indians ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He takes over the position from Mahela Jayawardene, who has stepped down. Pollard expressed his gratitude for the opportunity and emphasised his connection to the team. The franchise is hopeful that Pollard will help restore their winning form. Mumbai Indians aims to build on their past successes and inspire their fans.

articles.title: ‘Dissatisfied? You're not alone’: FIR filed over posters in Delhi Metro questioning govt
18-year-old Anahat's historic run at Silicon Valley Open comes to an end
articles.summary: India’s Anahat Singh exited the Silicon Valley Open after losing 3-1 to Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam despite winning the opening game. Sivasangari praised the 18-year-old’s talent and potential after staging a comeback. Anahat had earlier defeated world No. 14 Salma Hany to become the first Indian woman since 2019 to reach a PSA Tour Gold-level semifinal.

articles.title: 'Now is the time': Rubio warns Cuba next after Iran, asks Cubans to join hands
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Cubans to collaborate with intelligence agencies for positive change. He criticized the Cuban regime for corruption and unmet promises, suggesting this moment is crucial for action. The CIA later released a recruitment video encouraging Cubans to provide information discreetly. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump mentioned potential military actions nearby, heightening tensions over the situation.

articles.title: Over 100 detained as SIR protests continue in Delhi
articles.summary: Hundreds of protesters including students and farmers gathered in Delhi to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They criticized the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls for resulting in unfair voter deletions. Many demonstrators were detained by police as tensions escalated during the protest. Demonstrations have been organized in 88 cities across 18 states involving numerous organizations.

articles.title: Delhi HC junks Neha Bora plea against peace bond notice
articles.summary: The Delhi high court has denied AISA president Neha Bora's request to challenge a peace bond notice, which was raised amid concerns of potential peace disruption in a busy commercial district. The court determined that the special executive magistrate had enough evidence to issue the notice against Bora, who is facing several FIRs from the Delhi Police regarding public order violations.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi gig gets police nod amid fresh threats
articles.summary: With security concerns arising, the Delhi Police initially refused to grant permission for Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert. Following constructive discussions with the organisers, improved safety protocols were established, including the addition of 1,500 personnel for crowd management. Attendees will be updated about transportation options in collaboration with cab providers. The concert is officially rescheduled for October 30 at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

articles.title: Haryana power cut: Homes in dark for hours, residents block roads
articles.summary: A two-day power strike in Haryana caused significant disruptions across Gurgaon and surrounding areas. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini assured employees that no private power distribution licenses would be permitted. Outages led to water supply disruptions and industrial production halts, impacting many residents and businesses. Appeals were made by industry bodies for urgent government intervention to restore power.

articles.title: ITBP Raising Day: PM Modi praises ‘Himveers’ as India-China border remains in focus
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other leaders extended their greetings to ITBP personnel on the occasion. They praised the courage and sacrifices made by the force in protecting India's borders. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted the contributions of ITBP towards internal security and border safeguarding. Meanwhile, the Indian Army and Home Minister Amit Shah also conveyed their regards.

articles.title: 15-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Telangana; 7 arrested
articles.summary: Seven individuals, including three minors, were arrested in Siddipet district for allegedly assaulting a 15-year-old girl. The incident occurred on Dasara when the victim's parents were away for agricultural work. The accused reportedly took the girl to a neighboring village and returned her the following morning. The victim identified the perpetrators, leading her father to file a police complaint.

articles.summary: Down payment is only part of the money a buyer needs. Stamp duty, registration, moving expenses and furnishing can add to the upfront cost.

articles.summary: For Gowardhan, a dairy brand from Parag Milk Foods, Saif Ali Khan's candid humour turned into a free ad. Thanks to Saif, netizens said Gowardhan has become their top-of-mind ghee brand.

articles.title: Who is Matthew VanDyke and what is next in Myanmar arms training case as court allow him to stay in US till February?
articles.summary: A Delhi court extended until February 24 permission for US national Matthew VanDyke and six Ukrainians to remain abroad while the NIA investigates allegations that they trained ethnic armed groups in Myanmar. VanDyke, who received default bail in September, was also allowed to return to the US.

articles.title: 'Who's responsible for this mess in the first place?' Piyush Goyal ozone layer video goes viral from Berlin discussion
articles.summary: Piyush Goyal criticised Europe’s carbon emissions and accused developed nations of failing to deliver promised climate finance. He also warned that the EU’s carbon tax on steel could raise living costs and weaken its industries’ competitiveness.

articles.title: Barack Obama enters US midterm battleground: Can he help Democrats flip Senate seats in Ohio and Michigan?
articles.summary: Barack Obama returns to the campaign trail in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic Senate candidates as Republicans battle to retain control of the US Senate ahead of the 2026 midterm elect

articles.title: Delhi food safety ghee raid: Over 322 kg of ghee seized from stores; here's what was found, what you should be aware of
articles.summary: Delhi officials seized over 322 kg of ghee from stores offering steep festive discounts amid quality concerns. While lab results are awaited, consumers have been urged to check packaging and manufacturing and expiry dates before buying.

articles.title: German traveller reveals 10 things she wishes she knew before travelling to India as a solo traveller
articles.summary: A German vlogger’s viral video offers advice for women traveling alone in India. Her tips cover affordable transport and mobile data, visas, food delivery, hostels, and navigating local customs. She said her own experiences with street food and Indian hospitality were positive.

articles.title: Odisha Police Ganjam Gambling Crackdown, Raids: 470 arrested, over  ₹12.65 lakh seized ahead of Kumar Purnima
articles.summary: Odisha Police arrested 470 people in two days during a crackdown on gambling ahead of Kumar Purnima in Ganjam and Berhampur. Officers also seized cash and busted gambling dens as authorities warned that enforcement would continue.

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Melania Trump brokers localised ceasefire in Oleshky; all you need to know about the starving city
articles.summary: Melania Trump announced a localised Russia-Ukraine ceasefire to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where mines, drone attacks and damaged infrastructure have left residents struggling to access food and escape safely.

articles.title: IndiGo and Akasa Air extend Saudi flight suspensions: Check new dates; has Air India followed suit?
articles.summary: IndiGo flights to Riyadh remain cancelled until October 31 and services to three other Saudi cities until October 27. Akasa Air has extended its suspensions to Jeddah and Riyadh until November 10 and 30, respectively.

articles.title: Petrol and diesel prices today, October 24: Check fuel cost in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru
articles.summary: Brent oil finished out the week at the highest level since April as intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia added to supply concerns already stoked by the US-Iran war.

articles.title: Amid El Niño and fears of prolonged drought, Telangana announces 4-month employment scheme
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy announced a four-month employment scheme starting after Sankranti to support workers. With reservoirs critically low and many pump sets dry, the government will monitor water supplies, provide cattle fodder and drinking water, and create additional workdays.

articles.title: The week in charts: FPI selloff, Reliance bets, Blinkit’s expansion plans
articles.summary: In this weekly Plain Facts compilation, we present to you data-based insights, with easy-to-read charts, to help you delve deeper into the stories reported by Mint in the week gone by.

articles.title: Earthquake today: Magnitude 7.2 quake strikes waters near Vanuatu; triggers tsunami warning
articles.summary: The tsunami warning was later lifted. The magnitude of the earthquake was also revised to 6.9, down from an earlier estimate of 7.2 magnitude

articles.title: US ends tariffs on some Canadian products, replaces them with others amid tight mid-term race for Susan Collin in Maine
articles.summary: President Donald Trump will ease 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry-related imports starting October 30, while adding other Canadian goods to the tariff list. The change comes as trade tensions and rising costs affect border-state economies and shape a close Maine Senate race.

articles.title: FBI detains gangster Himanshu Bhau, India may get custody soon
articles.summary: Himanshu Bhau, a notorious gangster from north India, was recently captured by the FBI in Las Vegas. He has been wanted for a series of violent offenses, including multiple murders and extortion schemes that have plagued Delhi and Haryana. After escaping juvenile detention in 2020, he maintained his criminal operations through illegal networks.

articles.title: Israel launches ‘limited counterterrorism’ op after 2 IDF troops killed in West Bank
articles.summary: In a post on X, the IDF said, "In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell, and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged." The military said residents in areas where its forces are operating would be allowed to leave through three designated exit points.

articles.title: Fire engulfs Hitler’s teahouse ‘Eagle’s Nest’ in Germany; man arrested on arson suspicion
Watch: Giant waves crash into Taiwan as Typhoon Champi leaves over 500 injured; 1 dead
articles.summary: Typhoon Champi made landfall in Taiwan, resulting in one casualty and more than 500 injuries reported. The storm brought heavy rain and strong winds, leading to widespread power outages affecting over 167,000 homes. Over 240 flights were canceled due to severe weather conditions impacting transport services. Schools and offices were closed for an extended period as a precautionary measure against the storm.

articles.title: 'We have to think about posting 350 first': Rauf on need for bigger totals
articles.summary: Haris Rauf said his role alongside Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah is to take wickets and strengthen Pakistan’s bowling attack. He stressed teamwork, middle-over breakthroughs and the need for bigger totals as ODI cricket becomes more aggressive. Rauf is also focusing on improving his pace and fitness, while backing Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to contribute runs in upcoming matches.

articles.title: Ryan Gosling and Eva Mendes bought retreat made from 200-year-old barns in 2014
articles.summary: In 2014, Ryan Gosling and Eva Mendes purchased a distinctive rustic estate in Carpinteria, California. This property, crafted by Joel Schumacher, is constructed from reclaimed wood of three 200-year-old barns. Designed for privacy and a serene connection to nature, it embodies American history, offering a tranquil retreat from Los Angeles. The couple cherishes their family life away from the spotlight, valuing their children and preserving the estate's unique features.

articles.title: Krasinski and Emily Blunt sell Brooklyn apartment for $6.5M, net $1.5M profit
articles.summary: John Krasinski and Emily Blunt have sold their nearly 1,600-square-foot apartment at The Standish in Brooklyn Heights for $6.5 million. A trust linked to the couple purchased the property for $5 million in January 2024. The off-market sale, completed in June 2026, represents a $1.5 million increase in value in just over two years.

articles.title: Dan vs Daniel: Trump admin sues to block Alaska result if GOP candidate loses race
articles.summary: The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Alaska on Thursday, argues that the state must protect the integrity of federal elections. It asks the court to block the certification of a Peltola victory if Daniel Sullivan, a candidate from the small fishing community of Petersburg, remains on the ballot. “The United States accordingly brings this lawsuit to protect the integrity of the 2026 Senate election in Alaska,” the lawsuit says.

articles.title: Video: Gunmen storm Jordan church during funeral, killing 7 and wounding 40
articles.summary: Jordan's government described the attackers as unknown assailants and said investigations were moving ahead at full speed. It did not immediately confirm whether any suspects had been arrested or killed. Footage aired by Jordanian state television showed two men appearing to carry pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and opened fire before all three ran towards the building.

articles.title: Tom Brady helped provide 750,000 meals to families in need in Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen donated funds to provide 750,000 meals through Feeding Tampa Bay, supporting children, families and senior citizens in need. The contribution came shortly after the couple moved to Florida, where Brady began his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after 20 seasons with the New England Patriots. Their donation helped address food insecurity and supported local families facing financial hardship, highlighting their commitment to their new community.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Will Ishan Kishan's injury be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's gain?
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I match against New Zealand due to a strain. The team management has added uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra as a replacement in the squad. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may finally get an opportunity to play after being on the sidelines for nine matches. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak emphasized the need for patience regarding Sooryavanshi's exposure to international cricket.

articles.title: Shreyas Iyer on verge of breaking Rohit Sharma's unique T20I captaincy record
articles.summary: Iyer, who took over as India's T20I captain from Suryakumar Yadav in June, has scored 632 runs in 22 matches as skipper this year.

articles.title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms
articles.summary: The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30. The United States and Canada have closely connected economies.

articles.title: Cabinet secretariat merely acknowledged complaint of Election Commissioners': RTI

articles.title: ‘A racist terror attack’: Emmanuel Macron condemns deadly shooting near Paris
articles.summary: "These people were targeted because of their skin colour or perceived religion, and for no other reason," Macron said after meeting officials and residents in Trappes. "There is no place for this in France." Macron also said the suspect's statements indicated that the attack had been planned in advance. Police arrested the suspect less than 20 minutes after the shooting began.

articles.title: Odisha moves Supreme Court against Andhra Pradesh over rural poll notice in Kotia area

articles.summary: On October 17, a stampede broke out at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, claiming 19 lives. The pandal, erected in a narrow space with dim lighting, was filled with people soon after it started raining. Shrabana Chatterjee and Shiv Sahay Singh report on the lapses that led to the tragedy and the questions it has raised about accountability in West Bengal, where the new government’s first Durga Puja celebrations have been marred by controversy

articles.summary: Northeast monsoon began over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, South Interior Karnataka, and Kerala and Mahe.

articles.summary: The FBI has arrested Himanshu Bhau, a 24-year-old Indian gangster wanted in Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh for crimes including murder, extortion and kidnapping. Accused of leading a major gang and operating from abroad, Bhau is a rival of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi.

articles.title: A 4.5 magnitude earthquake struck Tibet on Saturday morning, days after a powerful quake killed 16
articles.summary: Two days after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet, killing at least 16 people, a magnitude 4.5 earthquake struck the region on Saturday (local time).

articles.title: Trump promises mortgage relief ahead of US midterms, but will American homeowners actually save? Explained
articles.summary: Trump's new mortgage relief order promises lower housing costs ahead of US midterms. Find out who qualifies, potential savings and why experts remain cautious.

articles.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
articles.summary: OpenAI will cut frontier models off from the internet weeks after one of its engineers said that solution wouldn't work.

articles.title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
articles.summary: PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.

articles.title: Cuba next? Trump hints at 'little stopover' after US warships return from Iran war
articles.summary: Trump and Rubio have both adopted a hard line towards Cuba's communist government. In May, the two renewed the possibility of US military intervention, with the threat gaining further significance after the Trump administration announced criminal charges against former Cuban leader Raúl Castro. Trump had floated a similar idea earlier this year but had not raised it publicly in recent months.

articles.title: China’s patrolling deviations disturb border: MEA on ITBP DG's face-offs remark
articles.summary: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time. The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.

articles.title: Upper layer NBFCs have to list: RBI guv on Tatas; dispels doubts on Sept order
articles.summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra’s comments also suggest Tata Sons is in breach of RBI rules. The consequences of continued noncompliance remain unclear. The governor declined to be drawn into the question of Noel Tata’s proposal to merge two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company, a move that could help it sidestep a stock market listing.

articles.title: Cabinet Secretary didn’t act on EC’ plaint as it was unofficial: RTI
articles.summary: According to documents shared as part of an RTI response, two ECs in their separate but near-identical letters to Somanathan on July 29 objected to Garg’s conduct and an order he issued revising allocation of work among senior officers. The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned.

articles.title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals
articles.summary: In a letter dated Oct 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them, including items used in cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (CTVS), neurosurgery and other clinical services. The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

articles.title: Need to unite against divisive forces, tackle new challenges: PM Modi
articles.summary: Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan, he said Swami Chinmayananda set his goals as per issues facing the country at the time and new challenges had emerged in the past few decades. “We must unite society against divisive forces. We must inspire citizens toward self-reliance, and we must connect every individual to vision of a developed India by 2047. For these objectives, we must become more proactive,” he said.

articles.title: Ukrainian soldier cuts off his own foot to survive, rescued by drone after 8 months
articles.summary: Kostiantyn Vlasenko, 49, had been stranded in a boiler room with severe injuries after a Russian drone strike. With no way to escape and little hope of being rescued, he made a desperate decision to amputate his remaining foot to survive. On October 4, a large drone lifted him into the air using a harness and carried him 15km to safety.

articles.title: Chloë Grace Moretz bought LA home at 19 for $3.4m, sold it for $5.65m
articles.summary: Chloë Grace Moretz purchased a $3.4 million home in Studio City in 2016 and hosted numerous gatherings there. After seven years, she listed the property for almost $6 million and sold it for $5.65 million. The home features multiple entertainment spaces, a separate studio, and luxurious outdoor areas. Studio City remains a popular area for high-profile buyers, including Olivia Wilde, who sold her property in December 2025.

articles.title: LA couple bought $925,000 farm, made barn a home, started cider business
articles.summary: David Bailey and Dana Tiel left their advertising careers to purchase a 16-acre farm in California. After spending $1 million, they converted a barn loft into their home. Their farm, Sierra Cider, includes a petting zoo, pumpkin patch and cider tastings. The couple faced challenges while balancing work and renovations during their transition. Despite initial doubts, the farm has become a popular destination for families and children.

articles.title: Slack co-founder bought Aspen estate for $25m, listed for $45m, sold for $30m
articles.summary: Stewart Butterfield and Jen Rubio recently finalized the sale of their Aspen estate for $30 million, right after their separation. They originally acquired the property for around $25 million in January 2021, yielding a nice profit despite initially aiming for $45 million. The estate has been purchased by David and Erika Sands, professional poker players, who now add it to their diverse real estate holdings across New York and California.

articles.title: Opposition's 'mock Parliament' to step up fight against SIR & CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: Sources said a “mock” gathering depicting an assembly of MPs may take place in the national capital on Oct 28. The event will involve MPs and others, but is unlikely to be a large gathering, given that a massive show of strength to push for the CEC’s resignation is planned at Ramlila Maidan as a “Delhi chalo” rally.

articles.title: Arms training case: US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24
articles.summary: VanDyke attended the court hearing Friday and sought the release of his seized personal articles. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training the insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.

articles.title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
articles.summary: In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.

articles.title: Brics parliamentary meet should end with joint statement: LS Speaker Om Birla
articles.summary: Talking to reporters Friday, Birla said the forum in India would work towards consensus-based dialogue on the role of Parliament in strengthening institutions, promotion of human-centred innovation in AI and digital technologies through Parliament, more representative system of global governance and role of Parliament in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for Brics countries.

articles.title: New norms for cars from 2029: Rear-crash tests, data recorders
articles.summary: The ministry has set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers. The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards. In a notification, the ministry also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from Oct 2029.

articles.title: After Op Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
articles.summary: Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijan’s ties with Pakistan — as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year — and India’s defence ties with Armenia. While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also discussed.

articles.title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
articles.summary: Coming ahead of India’s peak pollution season, the paper, titled ‘Air quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in India’, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La Niña/El Niño conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.

articles.title: Record growth, rising risks: What’s really driving India’s core industries? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.summary:
India’s core industrial sectors recorded a series-high growth rate of 7.9% in September, driven by strong performances in coal, electricity, steel and refinery products.

While the data points to a welcome industrial uptick, concerns remain about how sustainable the momentum will be. Much of the growth appears linked to temporary factors such as increased power demand during the heat wave and higher refining activity driven by imported oil.

With global crude prices rising, foreign exchange pressures mounting and infrastructure spending continuing to shoulder much of the growth burden, economists are questioning whether the current surge can be sustained in the coming months.

articles.title: Iran claims 7 oil tankers damaged in Hormuz, warns strikes if US helps passage

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Where India stands in medal tally after best day with 7 golds

articles.title: Marine life on the brink? 96% of coral reefs could face collapse by 2075
articles.summary: The International Union for Conservation of Nature recently highlighted the alarming vulnerability of coral reefs, predicting that by 2075, nearly all shallow-water coral systems may collapse due to rising ocean temperatures. This impending crisis threatens not only marine biodiversity but also the local communities that depend on these ecosystems for their livelihoods.

articles.title: Connecticut wool mill that lost 85 jobs now employs 50, makes military fabric
articles.summary: A Connecticut wool mill that closed in 2013, leaving 85 workers jobless, has been revived by former investment banker Jacob Harrison Long. He bought the 475,000-square-foot factory in 2014 despite having no manufacturing experience. Twelve years later, the mill employs about 50 people and supplies fabric for US military uniforms. Long now hopes to expand textile manufacturing across New England.

articles.title: Newton's 1687 book on gravity, funded by Halley, sold for Rs 5.49 crore
articles.summary: In a significant auction event, a first edition of Isaac Newton's *Philosophiæ naturalis principia mathematica* garnered an impressive US$576,000. This pivotal work introduced revolutionary concepts of motion and gravity through mathematical frameworks. With ties to distinguished scholars like the Kennet family and the vital endorsement from Edmond Halley, Newton's insights continue to resonate in disciplines such as engineering and astronomy, shaping modern scientific thought.

articles.title: Minnesota court reverses $20,000 privacy award in driveway camera feud

However, the appeals court overturned the privacy ruling, necessitating further proceedings and adjusting the damages for tree removal.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo reportedly invested $70 million in real estate in 2025

articles.title: Maldives begins planting coral on 2 submerged planes to build artificial reef

The project aims to combine marine tourism with aviation history while promoting coral growth. Various organizations are collaborating to monitor the ecological impact of this initiative.

articles.title: Frankfurt’s fitted kitchens turn 100; volunteers save parts from about 50

Today, preservationists are dedicated to conserving the remaining kitchens, adapting them with modern appliances while respecting their historical integrity.

articles.title: Why some couples are comfortable with silence, according to psychology
articles.summary: Silence in romantic relationships can signal comfort or discomfort based on personal communication styles and emotional needs. The 2024 study revealed that chosen silence often indicates emotional security and closeness. Alternatively, silence resulting from anxiety or hostility may lead to misunderstandings and emotional distance. Understanding each other's preferences regarding conversation and quiet time can strengthen relationships. Ultimately, intimacy is shaped by both meaningful conversations and moments of peaceful silence.

articles.title: Rare 1896 Chaucer book with 87 woodcuts sold for Rs 2.68 crore

With only about 50 deluxe copies ever bound, this book's rarity and artistic illustrations by Edward Burne-Jones continue to captivate collectors, emphasizing the allure of beautifully crafted literary works.

articles.title: Why some people struggle to say no even when exhausted, according to psychology

This habit stems from a fear of disappointing others, which can make saying no feel uncomfortable. Continued agreement may cause emotional exhaustion and hinder personal relationships. Effective strategies for setting boundaries include pausing before answering requests and practicing refusal in low-pressure situations.

articles.title: US soldier killed at 17 in Korean War identified after 75 years, to be buried
articles.summary: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.

articles.title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
articles.summary: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO says Starlink is helping win customers; Musk responds

articles.summary: An 86-year-old man from Mineral Wells, Texas, has been building a 62-foot steel boat since 1987. After three visitors discovered his ambition, they launched a crowdfunding campaign to support the project. More than $41,000 has been raised towards completing the boat and moving it to a launch site. The remaining work on the vessel is expected to require about $50,000 in funding.

Despite these challenges, he cleared 2.05m, setting a new Games record. His previous record was 1.95m in the T44 category. Praveen aims to defend his Paralympic title at the next Los Angeles Games.

articles.title: 'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'

Both leaders discussed expanding economic opportunities through the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. Tusk emphasized the positive economic developments achieved by Poland and India over the last 35 years.

articles.title: Exhibition row: Raihan recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down

While Vadra proposed removing select images, the officials demanded the removal of all 70 photographs, including those depicting the Indian national flag. This sparked outrage among Congress members, igniting debates about censorship and the value of artistic freedom.

articles.title: Pala-era Vishnu sculpture sold for Rs 8.16 crore, over 9 times estimate
articles.summary: A blackstone sculpture of Vishnu, dating to the 11th or 12th century, sold for £635,000 at Christie’s auction. The sculpture was previously part of a Swiss collection and first sold in March 1973. Over the years, the artwork maintained its significance and desirability among collectors. In June 2026, it was auctioned again as part of a collection focusing on South Asian art.

articles.title: China's restored reefs hold 286 oysters per sq m; particles down 62%
articles.summary: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness.

articles.title: Georgia woman loses marijuana smoke case as court upholds pension fund immunity
articles.summary: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.

articles.title: Delhi-NCR pollution: How GRAP Stage 1 curbs can protect your heart and lungs

Health experts stress the importance of immediate intervention to guard vulnerable populations against the health implications of poor air quality. articles.title: 'Vidhan Sabha uda diya': Bengaluru police arrest Bihar man over AI video

The video depicted a bomb blast at Vidhana Soudha, the Karnataka government's seat. The suspect, Hazrat Ali Shoiab, had been working as a daily-wage pipefitter in the city. Police discovered the footage during routine digital surveillance and tracked down the suspect's account. Investigations are ongoing to understand Shoiab's motives and identify any collaborators.

articles.title: Was Tiger Shroff the real target? | Pulse Maharashtra
articles.summary:
A celebrity shootout in Mumbai has sent shockwaves through the financial capital and has spread fear in the Hindi film industry. This wasn’t the first shootout in the city this year. And now, the industry is scared of the dark shadows of the past, when the underworld called the shots in Bollywood. And just like the past, this time too, the masterminds seem to be operating from foreign shores. But was Tiger Shroff the real target? Is this shootout related to incidents like the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique, the shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence and the reported threats to actors Ranveer Singh and Aamir Khan?

In this week’s Pulse Maharashtra with Vinaya Deshpande, we take you through what we know so far and what the unanswered questions are. And how this attack leads to an old fear in the heart of an industry which is one of India’s greatest soft powers in the world – Bollywood.

articles.title: CJP leaders released after court rejects police plea for extended custody

After spending seven days in jail, Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been released following an order by a Special Executive Magistrate court in Delhi.

The two leaders were detained after the October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar and had been held in judicial custody while police sought preventive action against them. The court eventually ordered their release after they submitted undertakings promising not to organise protests at Jantar Mantar while the site remains denotified and not to disturb public peace.

articles.title: eMudhra security breach: What it means for smartphone, internet users

Browser companies like Google, Apple, Microsoft, and Mozilla responded by blocking these certificates rapidly. eMudhra explained that a flaw during the creation process led to the publication of the weak keys. Importantly, no evidence suggests these weak keys were used in actual attacks so far.
